newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares edge up at noon in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares edge up at noon in thin trade.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares edged higher in morning trading on Friday on thin volume, with many investors waiting for fresh news, brokers said.

Although the B share index ended Friday morning in positive territory, activity was relatively thin as investors were more interested in subscribing to new share issues than buying stocks on the secondary market, they said.
The B index gained 0.023 points or 0.03 percent to 76.471 points on volume of 3.065 million shares worth $1.496 million.
"Volume was light because there are some foreign investors waiting for new issues," said an analyst at an Asian securities firm in Shanghai.
Inner Mongolia Yitai Coal Co said on Friday it would begin issuing 166 million B shares priced at $0.4073 each.

The subscription period for Shanghai Zhenhua Port Machinery Co's 100 million B share offering, priced at $0.433 per share, ended on Thursday and more initial public offerings were in the pipeline, brokers said.

"The market has entered a consolidation period," said a broker at a foreign securities firm. "Two new B shares issues and some rights issues drained large amounts of capital from the secondary market."

"The recent rise in the Hong Kong stock market has also drawn foreign investors' attention away from the B share market, while domestic investors are cautious due to uncertainties over interim reports," he said.
Of 45 B shares, 32 traded with 11 up, 11 flat and 10 down.
Shanghai Dazhong Taxi Co was the most actively traded B share on institutional buying, gaining $0.010 or 1.16 percent to $0.872 on volume of 335,000 shares.
Shanghai's A share index also inched up on some speculative buying by major market players, but trading was not active due to cautious market sentiment, brokers said.
The A index gained 1.954 points or 0.16 percent to 1,253.968 points on volume of 207.858 million shares worth 2.726 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index lost 4.263 points or 0.11 percent to 3,870.206 points.
